purpose: Published CORD-v2 test score of R2 (Qwen3.5-2B LoRA, 3 epochs, merged), compared with R0 (Nemotron-Parse v1.1 full SFT) on the same images; checkpoint chosen on validation, never on test

model.train_data: CORD-v2 train as a local image folder (data/reference/cord-v2-train), target = gt_parse JSON
model.prompt: Read this receipt and return its fields as JSON.

checkpoint_choice.rule: LOWEST_VAL wins only if its paired CI vs LATEST excludes 0, else LATEST (research, 2026-10-13)
checkpoint_choice.note: 181 ran as base + adapter, 272 as merged weights; the difference may include merge effects, the decision is unchanged

code.scorer: vlm_pipeline.eval.cord (field_f1_counts on the dict read by json_answer: outermost JSON object, parse failure = empty prediction)
code.note: worker ran from a clean worktree; run.json git_dirty=True describes the shared main tree

decoding.generation_config: none in the base snapshot -> transformers defaults (repetition_penalty 1.0)

vs_r0.method: paired bootstrap over the same 100 test images (1000 resamples, seed 0), field F1 on the same ground truth
fairness_notes: R0 answers Donut-style CORD tokens (read with token2json), R2 answers JSON (read with json_answer); both are scored as dicts with the same field F1
R0: full SFT 3 epochs (300 steps); R2: LoRA 3 epochs then merged; one training seed each, run-to-run variance not measured
R0 is the app default by user decision; both numbers are published

speed: 582 s for 100 images including model load (~10 images/min, HF bf16, batch 1, GB10); R0 Parse ~7 images/min
ci_method: bootstrap over images, 1000 resamples, seed 0, micro F1 from per-image (tp, errors) counts

vs_base.note: the base answers valid JSON in its own schema (keys like ticket/items), so it scores 0 field F1 on CORD's schema: the delta measures learning the target format and values, not reading ability alone
